bandwidth</a></li></ul></div></nav><div class="prose prose--block prose--blog col-span-full!"><p>Cursor can now respond by creating canvases to visually represent information. This allows you to explore and interact with custom interfaces instead of reading walls of texts in chats or markdown files that can be hard to digest.</p>
<p>With canvases, agents can create dashboards for real-world data as well as custom interfaces with logic and interactivity tailored to your request. Agents can use them to help you review PRs, learn new libraries, or even manage other agents in Cursor. In the <a href="https://cursor.com/docs/agent/agents-window" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Agents Window</a>, canvases are durable artifacts that live alongside your other tools like the terminal, browser, and source control.</p>
<h2 id="components-as-building-blocks" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#components-as-building-blocks" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Components as building blocks</h2>
<p>Cursor renders canvases using a React-based UI library with first-party components like tables, boxes, diagrams, and charts. We gave agents access to existing components in Cursor like diffs and to-do lists, and we also instructed it to follow data visualization best practices.</p>
<p>You can create skills to teach agents how to create different kinds of canvases. For example, the <a href="https://cursor.com/marketplace/cursor/docs-canvas" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Docs Canvas skill</a> allows Cursor to generate an interactive architecture diagram of your repo.</p>
<h2 id="how-we-use-canvases-at-cursor" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#how-we-use-canvases-at-cursor" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>How we use canvases at Cursor</h2>
<p>We&#x27;ve found canvases particularly useful for data-intensive tasks. They allow agents to arrange information in a way that&#x27;s non-linear and easier to digest than plain text.</p>
<h3 id="incident-response-dashboard" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#incident-response-dashboard" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Incident response dashboard</h3>
<p><a href="https://cursor.com/marketplace/datadog" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Datadog</a>, <a href="https://cursor.com/marketplace/databricks" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Databricks</a>, and <a href="https://cursor.com/marketplace/sentry" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Sentry</a> MCPs in Cursor have enabled us to dive into observability data with agents, which often find insights that we&#x27;d miss on our own. Before canvases, the agent would represent time-series data in a markdown table, which was hard to interpret and required additional steps to visualize.</p>
<p>Now, the agent can create visualizations in a canvas that join data from multiple sources, including local debug files, into a single chart.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/kMGs01X6Ar00THbfjzAzFC0237Det00efN1v9wiTJl5eFtE/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<h3 id="pr-review-interface" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#pr-review-interface" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>PR review interface</h3>
<p>We are reviewing larger diffs than ever before. Traditional tools present all changes equally, requiring us to figure out what parts of the diff are most important.</p>
<p>With canvases, Cursor can logically group changes together, prioritize what&#x27;s most important for you to review, and present a rich interface for you to explore the change set. It can even write pseudocode representations for tricky algorithms.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/5C7UDkyai2F6vGvAFPlfvq5CtO8KoNND5fD2e009JGO00/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<h3 id="eval-analysis" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#eval-analysis" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Eval analysis</h3>
<p>At Cursor, we spend a lot of time investigating eval results as we make changes to our harness and release new models into the product. Previously, engineers had to inspect request IDs one at a time to identify patterns. We considered building and deploying a web app to automate this process, but instead, we operationalized it directly with a skill in Cursor.</p>
<p>The skill allows agents to read all of the rollouts in an eval, group failures, and build a canvas for investigating eval failures and cluster failure modes. This allows us to identify harness bugs that were hidden before, and recently helped us release two new models in Cursor with far less effort.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/hc7nzkB1Ty85DJMcGDj2w9P702aYdbA1GOj7MsfYj5QA/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<h3 id="autoresearch-experiment" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#autoresearch-experiment" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Autoresearch experiment</h3>
<p>We have been adapting the ideas in <a href="https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">autoresearch</a> to enable agents to tackle complex optimization challenges related to the performance of our clients. With canvases, the agent can visualize its research progress while running experiments, enabling the user to check on progress and see the hypothesis the agent is currently testing.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/elZg8pzS004gwJU701iZvZ7zdYu3x5cY2URWgiw3yEN3k/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<h2 id="increasing-information-bandwidth" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#increasing-information-bandwidth" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Increasing information bandwidth</h2>
<p>Recent improvements like <a href="https://cursor.com/changelog#design-mode" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Design Mode</a> and <a href="https://cursor.com/changelog#upgraded-voice-input" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">upgraded voice input</a> are all part of our effort to increase information bandwidth. We want to remove friction in human-agent collaboration and make it easier to express your intent beyond plain text.</p>
<p>Try canvases in <a href="https://cursor.com/download" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Cursor 3.1</a>, or learn more in <a href="https://cursor.com/docs/agent/tools/canvas" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">our docs</a>.</p></div><footer class="mt-v2"><p class="type-base"><span class="text-theme-text-sec">Filed under:<!-- --> </span><a class="text-theme-text bandwidth</a></li></ul></div></nav><div class="prose prose--block prose--blog col-span-full!"><p>Cursor can now respond by creating canvases to visually represent information. This allows you to explore and interact with custom interfaces instead of reading walls of texts in chats or markdown files that can be hard to digest.</p>
<p>With canvases, agents can create dashboards for real-world data as well as custom interfaces with logic and interactivity tailored to your request. Agents can use them to help you review PRs, learn new libraries, or even manage other agents in Cursor. In the <a href="https://cursor.com/docs/agent/agents-window" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Agents Window</a>, canvases are durable artifacts that live alongside your other tools like the terminal, browser, and source control.</p>
<h2 id="components-as-building-blocks" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#components-as-building-blocks" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Components as building blocks</h2>
<p>Cursor renders canvases using a React-based UI library with first-party components like tables, boxes, diagrams, and charts. We gave agents access to existing components in Cursor like diffs and to-do lists, and we also instructed it to follow data visualization best practices.</p>
<p>You can create skills to teach agents how to create different kinds of canvases. For example, the <a href="https://cursor.com/marketplace/cursor/docs-canvas" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Docs Canvas skill</a> allows Cursor to generate an interactive architecture diagram of your repo.</p>
<h2 id="how-we-use-canvases-at-cursor" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#how-we-use-canvases-at-cursor" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>How we use canvases at Cursor</h2>
<p>We&#x27;ve found canvases particularly useful for data-intensive tasks. They allow agents to arrange information in a way that&#x27;s non-linear and easier to digest than plain text.</p>
<h3 id="incident-response-dashboard" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#incident-response-dashboard" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Incident response dashboard</h3>
<p><a href="https://cursor.com/marketplace/datadog" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Datadog</a>, <a href="https://cursor.com/marketplace/databricks" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Databricks</a>, and <a href="https://cursor.com/marketplace/sentry" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Sentry</a> MCPs in Cursor have enabled us to dive into observability data with agents, which often find insights that we&#x27;d miss on our own. Before canvases, the agent would represent time-series data in a markdown table, which was hard to interpret and required additional steps to visualize.</p>
<p>Now, the agent can create visualizations in a canvas that join data from multiple sources, including local debug files, into a single chart.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/kMGs01X6Ar00THbfjzAzFC0237Det00efN1v9wiTJl5eFtE/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<h3 id="pr-review-interface" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#pr-review-interface" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>PR review interface</h3>
<p>We are reviewing larger diffs than ever before. Traditional tools present all changes equally, requiring us to figure out what parts of the diff are most important.</p>
<p>With canvases, Cursor can logically group changes together, prioritize what&#x27;s most important for you to review, and present a rich interface for you to explore the change set. It can even write pseudocode representations for tricky algorithms.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/5C7UDkyai2F6vGvAFPlfvq5CtO8KoNND5fD2e009JGO00/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<h3 id="eval-analysis" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#eval-analysis" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Eval analysis</h3>
<p>At Cursor, we spend a lot of time investigating eval results as we make changes to our harness and release new models into the product. Previously, engineers had to inspect request IDs one at a time to identify patterns. We considered building and deploying a web app to automate this process, but instead, we operationalized it directly with a skill in Cursor.</p>
<p>The skill allows agents to read all of the rollouts in an eval, group failures, and build a canvas for investigating eval failures and cluster failure modes. This allows us to identify harness bugs that were hidden before, and recently helped us release two new models in Cursor with far less effort.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/hc7nzkB1Ty85DJMcGDj2w9P702aYdbA1GOj7MsfYj5QA/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<h3 id="autoresearch-experiment" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#autoresearch-experiment" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Autoresearch experiment</h3>
<p>We have been adapting the ideas in <a href="https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">autoresearch</a> to enable agents to tackle complex optimization challenges related to the performance of our clients. With canvases, the agent can visualize its research progress while running experiments, enabling the user to check on progress and see the hypothesis the agent is currently testing.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/elZg8pzS004gwJU701iZvZ7zdYu3x5cY2URWgiw3yEN3k/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<h2 id="increasing-information-bandwidth" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#increasing-information-bandwidth" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Increasing information bandwidth</h2>
<p>Recent improvements like <a href="https://cursor.com/changelog#design-mode" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Design Mode</a> and <a href="https://cursor.com/changelog#upgraded-voice-input" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">upgraded voice input</a> are all part of our effort to increase information bandwidth. We want to remove friction in human-agent collaboration and make it easier to express your intent beyond plain text.</p>
<p>Try canvases in <a href="https://cursor.com/download" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Cursor 3.1</a>, or learn more in <a href="https://cursor.com/docs/agent/tools/canvas" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">our docs</a>.</p></div><footer class="mt-v2"><p class="type-base"><span class="text-theme-text-sec">Filed under:<!-- --> </span><a class="text-theme-text
